response_description: The NPI‑Q is a brief, informant‑completed version of the original Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI), designed to assess 12 neuropsychiatric symptom domains commonly associated with dementia and related neurocognitive disorders. It provides two types of scores: Symptom Severity Score Caregiver Distress Score There are 12 domains - each domain begins with a yes/no screening question. If answered yes, severity and distress are rated; Domains include: Delusions Hallucinations Agitation/Aggression Depression/Dysphoria Anxiety Euphoria Apathy Disinhibition Irritability/Lability Aberrant motor behaviour Night‑time disturbances Appetite/eating changes If a symptom is present, the informant rates how severe it has been in the last month: 0 = Not present, 1 = Mild, 2 = Moderate, 3 = Severe For each present symptom, caregivers rate their distress level - ranging from 0 = Not distressing at all to 5 = Extremely distressing The NPI‑Q produces two separate total scores.
